test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following agencies is responsible for formulating the fiscal policy of India?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Ministry of Finance of the Government of India
National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development

solution:
The correct answer is** Ministry of Finance of the Government of India**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Finance of the Government of India:**

 
 
• The Ministry of Finance is responsible for formulating and implementing the fiscal policy of India.
 
• This includes managing government revenue, expenditure, and overall financial management to ensure economic stability and growth.
 
• The Ministry of Finance oversees budget preparation, taxation policies, and public debt management, among other critical financial functions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India:**

 
 
• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates the securities market in India.
 
• Its primary function is to protect investor interests and promote the development of the securities market.
 
• SEBI does not formulate fiscal policy; its role is more focused on market regulation and oversight.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India:**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of the country and is responsible for monetary policy, not fiscal policy.
 
• RBI manages the country's money supply and interest rates to control inflation and stabilize the currency.
 
• While RBI plays a crucial role in economic stability, it does not handle fiscal policy formulation.
 
 
 
• **National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development:**
 
 
• The National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD) focuses on the development of agriculture and rural areas in India.
 
• Its functions include providing credit for agriculture, small-scale industries, and other rural economic activities.
 
• NABARD does not formulate fiscal policy; its role is more specialized in rural development and agricultural finance.
